content.title: The April Pink Full Moon Is Rising Tonight — Here's When To See It In Australia
content.text: And, the astrological meaning of this moonrise Jenna Ortega's Best Fashion Moments0 seconds of 1 minute, 15 secondsVolume 0% THE RUNDOWN The April 2026 pink full moon will rise tonight Thursday, April 2, at 1:11 pm AEST. While the moon phase will reach its apex during the day in Australia, the moon will be full and radiant from around 7:30pm AEST. The pink moon is not actually “pink”; it takes its name from traditional agricultural practices in North America. Last month, we were transfixed by the spectacle of the lunar eclipse, but this month will bring a gentler celestial offering: the pink full moon. April’s full moon rises tonight, Thursday, April 2nd 2026, the fourth of 2026’s thirteen full moons casting its soft glow just in time for the Easter long weekend. Known to astronomers as the Paschal Moon, this moon, thanks to the Western Christian tradition, determines the date of Easter, which falls on the first Sunday after the full moon and the spring equinox. The April pink full moon doesn’t carry the rosé flush its name suggests. It will, however, be luminous, low on the horizon and well worth stepping out for. Here’s everything you need to know about the April full moon, including exactly where and when to see it in Australia. When Is The 2026 April Pink Full Moon?April’s pink full moon will reach its apex at 1:11pm AEST on Thursday. In Australia, that moment falls in the middle of the afternoon, meaning the moon won’t be visible at its most technically complete. But, come nightfall, it will be glowing at full intensity and unmissable against a clear sky from around 7:30pm AEST. What Time Is The 2026 Pink Full Moon In Your Australian State Tonight The full moon will be fully visible as soon as the sky darkens in your state. Use the table below as your guide. City (Time Zone) Peak Time Best Viewing (After Sunset)Sydney (AEDT)11:11pm6:50pm Melbourne (AEDT) 1:11pm7:13pmBrisbane (AEST) 12:11pm 5:45pm Adelaide (ACDT)12:41pm 7:10pm Canberra (AEDT) 1:11pm 6:58pm Hobart (AEDT)1:11pm 7:01pm Darwin (ACST) 11:41am 6:49pm Perth (AWST) 10:11am 6:12pm Where To See The April Full Moon Tonight The full moon rewards the effort of escaping the city. Find an open space where the horizon stretches wide and artificial light retreats — a hilltop, a headland, a beach where the water will reflect the glow of the moon back to you. Pack a picnic blanket, let your eyes adjust to the dark, and look east. Image: Getty Phlox subulata sometimes referred to as “pink moss” which covers the ground in some regions. Why Is It Called The Pink Full Moon?The name is a little misleading. Unlike last month’s blood moon, April’s full moon won’t carry any rosy tint — unless there is air pollution, which can sometimes result in a hazy glow. It will be the same cool, luminous silver we’ve come to expect. Its name derives from North America, where many traditional moon names originated. The April moon heralded the arrival of spring and the blooming of Phlox subulata — a low, creeping wildflower that carpets the ground in a haze of pale pink. The name was recorded by sources including The Old Farmer’s Almanac, drawing on Native American, Colonial American and European traditions in which moons were named for the seasons and what they brought with them.Other cultures knew this moon differently:The Breaking Ice Moon (Algonquin): marking the thaw that returned mobility to frozen landscapesThe Budding Moon of Plants and Shrubs (Tlingit): a recognition of the plant world stirring back to lifeThe Sucker Moon (Anishinaabe): named for the sucker fish that returned to shallow waterways to spawnThis full moon also carries ecclesiastical significance. Sometimes called the Paschal Moon, it determines the dates of Easter and Passover — a rare convergence of the astronomical and the sacred. What Does The April Pink Full Moon Mean Spiritually? As well as being aligned with Christian orthodoxy this pink full moon has astrological meaning. According to astrologer Kristy Grey, the Libra moon is arriving on a potent Aries-Libra axis thanks to the Aries season. “We are working with the tension between the Sun in Aries (the ‘I am’—our core identity and dreams) and the Moon in Libra (the ‘We are’—our collaborations and connections),” says Gray. “Think of this lunar event as a ‘spring clean.’ Because Aries represents the self, it’s an invitation to put our own aspirations at the epicentre of our lives and audit everything else around them.” When Is The Next Full Moon? The next full moon is the Flower Moon, which marks the blooms across the Northern Hemisphere in May. It will rise on May 2.
